subject: Biotechnology
title: Mitochondrial Replacement Therapy
description: A 60-second lesson on Mitochondrial Replacement Therapy.

hook.text: Three-parent babies — mitochondrial replacement therapy prevents devastating diseases by combining DNA from three people.

buildup.text: Mitochondrial diseases affect 1 in 5,000 births — faulty mitochondria cause seizures, blindness, heart failure, and early death.

discovery.text: MRT swaps faulty mitochondria for healthy ones — the child has nuclear DNA from two parents and mitochondrial DNA from a donor.

twist.text: The UK legalized MRT in 2015 — the first country to approve a form of heritable human genetic modification.

climax.text: The first MRT baby was born in 2016 — but carried only 1% donor mitochondria, raising questions about long-term effectiveness.

punchline.text: Three genetic parents, one healthy child — MRT blurs boundaries while preventing tragedy.

quiz.question: Why is mitochondrial replacement therapy considered a form of heritable genetic modification?
options: It changes the child's nuclear DNA permanently
The donor mitochondrial DNA is passed to all future generations through the maternal line
It creates a genetically identical copy of the donor

details.summary: Mitochondrial replacement therapy prevents inherited mitochondrial diseases by combining nuclear DNA from the parents with healthy mitochondria from a donor egg. The resulting child has genetic material from three people, raising unique ethical and regulatory questions.
details.whyItMatters: MRT prevents devastating mitochondrial diseases affecting about 1 in 5,000 births. The UK became the first country to approve it in 2015. It crosses the germline boundary since mitochondrial DNA changes are heritable, creating regulatory precedent.
takeaways: MRT replaces defective mitochondria with healthy donor mitochondria
The resulting child inherits DNA from three people but 99.9% from parents
The UK approved MRT in 2015 as the first country to legalize the technique

faq.question: Does MRT really create three-parent babies?
faq.answer: Technically yes, but over 99.9 percent of DNA comes from the two parents. The donor contributes only 37 mitochondrial genes compared to roughly 20,000 nuclear genes. The donor's contribution affects energy metabolism but not traits like appearance or personality.

faq.question: Why is MRT ethically controversial despite preventing disease?
faq.answer: MRT modifies the germline because mitochondrial DNA is inherited maternally. Critics argue it opens the door to other heritable modifications. Supporters note it prevents severe suffering and the mitochondrial contribution is minimal compared to nuclear DNA.
